snippet: biggest LLM-related mistake, is trying to obviate three major things: 1. writing/developing a distinct authorial "voice" 2. learning financial statement analysis/modeling 3. reading books (1/4) …
content_text: biggest LLM-related mistake, is trying to obviate three major things: 1. writing/developing a distinct authorial "voice" 2. learning financial statement analysis/modeling 3. reading books (1/4) especially the first two, there really are no shortcuts -- its all reps its akin to going to a gym and saying, "grok go bench 225 for me" u will never develop any muscle if u never lift any weight the 3rd one, books, I've given up trying to explain is it possible that an 1000-page book could've been 900 pages, sure is it possible that an 1000-page book fits into "grok summarize this in 3 paragraphs"... absolutely not lol (2/4) but the way I now view it, its pointless trying to explain this to someone who doesn't want to listen especially when all that this does, is provide larger and larger advantages to people who DO read your competition is getting stupider and stupider they can generate a DCF but can't explain any of it their writing is identical to the writing of a 4-year old in rural Bangladesh, bc both "write" the exact same way (perfect English generated by an LLM) and now, on top of that, they are willing to concede to u everything that the great have put on paper over thousands of years (3/4) "what were seneca's letters about, summarize it for me grok" "they're about navigating life's vicissitudes and overcoming hardship" "ok add it all to my Skills.md, and add Market Wizards too" flaccid dork behavior its the same principle as how, when everyone else is emasculated on the couch swiping on dating apps...the few ppl just kicking game in broad daylight, theyre going to get an incrementally larger share of the pie inequality widens, nature becomes even more aristocratic this isn't to say that I don't have the same concerns as everyone else, about the dumbification of future generations...this tweet was one of the craziest things I have ever seen: -- "At Harvard, a student thought A Clockwork Orange was written in “Old English” and used AI to “translate” it. Others “view reading as an unnecessarily burdensome way of acquiring knowledge” and think professors who ask them to do it are “arbitrarily withholding information.” -- harvard kids can't comprehend a novel from 1962 truly mind-blowing...tolchocks u right in the litso (4/4) but, why worry about what u can't change let Darwinism do its thing people are gonna do whatever they feel like doing...if they don't wanna read books, ur not gonna make them read books. may as well focus on the 1% who are actually listening this is where u can really move the needle the gap is only getting wider, ppl with their head screwed on straight are going to start lapping motherfuckers at a crazy pace and u don't have to do much more than insert someone into the pre-configured chain of command "here's Montaigne, he writes well, and here's the two people who he actively read: Seneca and Plutarch" none of this shit ever changes, eminent dead from 500 years ago referencing eminent dead from 2000 years ago u can bet ur ass that over this time horizon, there have been many attempts made to take shortcuts, get abbreviated versions, summaries, Cliff's notes that's what people don't seem to understand u really dont think any student in the last 2500 years ever asked their teacher "hey, can we do the Book of Job in 5 chapters instead of 42?" and now u think grok can magically give it to u in 280 characters I'm not even gonna argue with ppl, this is exactly why I gave up just viddying from the sidelines now END Munger says "go where there's dumb competition" man...u don't even have to go anywhere they're actively getting dumber for u. shit is amazing bro, it really is best time in history to be a young philosopher-king 🙌
